meta.note: Demo deck — Jordan Lee @ Northwind Analytics

cards.question: Walk me through your background.
cards.referenceAnswer: Nine years in backend and data engineering. Last four at Relay Commerce where I led our streaming migration — cut data freshness from 18 hours to under five minutes — and built an ingestion SDK that twelve product teams adopted. Before that, CDC pipelines at DataFlow. I'm looking for staff-level platform scope; Northwind's ingestion challenge is exactly the kind of multi-team architecture work I want to own.
cards.myAnswer: I've been doing data eng for about 9 years. At Relay I led the move from batch to streaming and built our SDK. I want staff scope on platform.
cards.aiCoaching:
**Strong:** Clear arc and real metrics.

**Tighten:** Open with the 18h→5min hook in sentence one. Name Northwind's ingestion mission explicitly. Drop "about" — say nine years.

**Model opener:** "Nine years building data platforms — most recently I led Relay's streaming migration, cutting freshness from 18 hours to five minutes, then an SDK twelve teams adopted. I'm here because Northwind's platform guild is the product, not a sidecar."

cards.question: Tell me about a time you influenced without authority.
cards.referenceAnswer: Twelve teams had copy-pasted ingestion code causing drift and outages. I couldn't mandate a single SDK. I ran a pilot with three friendly teams, shipped semver and changelogs, held weekly office hours. Within eight months twelve teams migrated voluntarily. Platform NPS went from 42 to 71.

cards.question: How would you safely roll out a new event type to production?
cards.referenceAnswer: Schema review with producers, contract tests in CI, shadow traffic or dual-write to validate counts, feature flag per tenant, dashboard on lag and error rate, rollback path documented before cutover. Phased rollout — never big-bang all tenants.
cards.myAnswer: I'd add schema validation, test in staging, roll out gradually with feature flags and watch dashboards.
cards.aiCoaching: **Good skeleton.** Add contract tests between producer/consumer, dual-write validation period, and explicit rollback criteria. Mention tenant-scoped flags — matches Northwind multi-tenant context.

cards.question: Describe your streaming migration — hardest tradeoff?
cards.referenceAnswer: Hardest tradeoff was exactly-once vs operational complexity. We chose at-least-once with idempotent sinks and reconciliation jobs — simpler ops, acceptable for our SLA. Dual-write for six weeks let us validate counts before cutover; zero customer incidents during Black Friday.

cards.question: Why Northwind? Why leave Relay?
cards.referenceAnswer: Relay was the right place to grow into senior scope. Northwind is where the platform IS the bottleneck the company is hiring staff to fix — VP's blog post matched problems I've already solved at smaller scale. I want staff IC scope shaping guild direction, not to jump for a title alone.

cards.question: Product wants a shortcut that breaks schema standards. What do you do?
cards.referenceAnswer: Understand the deadline and user impact. Propose a time-boxed exception path with explicit tech debt ticket, narrower scope, and sunset date. Escalate to EM if it's a pattern. Document in RFC so guild sees precedent — never silent one-offs.
